expectations.name: single-function-in-isolation
expected_behavior: Runs straight through with no plan gate, mapping to the `Test_Parse` direct-test family
Measures with `-run '^Test_Parse($|_)'` and reads only `Parse`'s own line range — the coverage `Test_Load` contributes is not counted
Adds table rows aimed at the two error branches, re-measures, and confirms those lines went 0 → hit
New rows follow the style Test rules: `have`/`want`, never `got`; error subtests named `error - <condition>`

expectations.name: package-target-is-plan-first
expected_behavior: States the resolved kind (package) and the function set before measuring
Presents a plan — per-function current coverage, proposed easy cases, deferred and un-coverable lines — and waits for approval before writing anything

Works one function to completion before starting the next — a per-function after-profile exists for each (`<Func>.after`), alongside the `<Func>.before` the plan step wrote, each written after that function's tests and before the next function's, so the order is visible in the artifacts rather than asserted

Keeps the plan's before-measurements as distinct per-function files — every function in scope has its own `<Func>.before`, none overwritten by the next function's measurement, so the reported before-figures can be checked against a file

Reports how many cases were added, counted as `max_tests` counts them (one per table row or subtest), and that number equals the cases actually present in the tests-added list — even though this run carries no `max_tests`

expectations.name: deferred-and-uncoverable-are-reported
expected_behavior: Covers the easy lines, defers the network branch with a stated reason, and names the defensive branch un-coverable
Under `include=all`, builds the fake for the network branch and covers it
Still reports the defensive `return` as un-coverable under `include=all` — the flag does not turn it into an attempt
Classifies `MustDial`'s panic as easy and asserts it — a documented panic is a contract, not a panic-only path with no recoverable contract
Classifies `Retry`'s post-sleep line as complex and defers it, not as un-coverable: a test that waits does reach it, so nothing is unreachable and no seam is missing
Coins no test-name suffix beyond `Test_Foo` / `Test_Foo_tabular`, whatever suffixes the package's existing tests happen to carry
